source: USGS National Digital Trails / 3DEP Public Domain & OpenStreetMap ODbL

destinations.name: New Hampshire White Mountains
destinations.agency: USFS White Mountain National Forest, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: Alpine ridgelines, glacially carved ravines, waterfalls, and AMC high huts from Franconia Ridge across the Presidential Range to the Wildcats, Carters and Baldfaces at the Maine border, and north to Mount Cabot.

destinations.name: Yosemite Valley & High Country
destinations.agency: NPS Yosemite GIS, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: Granite monoliths, thundering waterfalls, and high-country rim loops from Happy Isles to Glacier Point and Half Dome.

destinations.name: Acadia National Park
destinations.agency: NPS Acadia GIS, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: Pink granite peaks rising straight from the Atlantic Ocean, historic iron-rung cliff trails, and glacial lakes.

destinations.name: Shenandoah National Park Central
destinations.agency: NPS Shenandoah GIS, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: Blue Ridge granite scrambles, Appalachian Trail ridge walks, and cascading hollow waterfalls.

destinations.name: Rocky Mountain National Park – Bear Lake Corridor
destinations.agency: NPS Rocky Mountain GIS, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: High-altitude glacial gorges, alpine cirque lakes, and Continental Divide tundra climbs between 9,475 ft and 12,324 ft.

destinations.name: Zion Canyon
destinations.agency: NPS Zion GIS, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: Soaring Navajo sandstone cliffs, Virgin River narrows, and carved canyon switchbacks.

destinations.name: Mount Rainier – Paradise Corridor
destinations.agency: NPS Mount Rainier GIS, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: Subalpine wildflower meadows, cascading waterfalls, and high-altitude viewpoints overlooking active glaciers.

destinations.name: Mount Monadnock
destinations.state_or_region: New Hampshire (Monadnock State Park — Jaffrey & Dublin)
destinations.agency: NH Division of Parks & Recreation, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: One of the most-climbed mountains in the world: a 3,165 ft bald summit with a dense web of short, steep, rocky trails from Jaffrey, Dublin and the Old Toll Road.

destinations.name: Fitchburg, Leominster & Princeton
destinations.state_or_region: Massachusetts (Fitchburg, Townsend, Westminster, Leominster & Princeton — with Pearl Hill, Willard Brook, Crow Hills & Wachusett Mountain)
destinations.agency: MA DCR, Mass Audubon, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: Rolling hemlock and pine woods, brooks and ponds north of Fitchburg: Pearl Hill, Table Rock, Trap Falls and a dense web of shared hiking and mountain-bike trails, linked by the Midstate Trail to Leominster State Forest, the Crow Hill Ledges and the town of Princeton, with Wachusett Mountain and Wachusett Meadow.

destinations.name: Acton, Boxborough & Harvard
destinations.state_or_region: Massachusetts (Acton, Boxborough & Harvard — with Nashoba Brook, Steele Farm, Holy Hill & the Oxbow refuge)
destinations.agency: Town Conservation Commissions, Harvard Conservation Trust, USFWS, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: Gentle hills, orchards, stone walls and brooks west of Concord: a patchwork of town conservation lands from Acton's Nashoba Brook and Great Hill through Boxborough's Steele Farm and Beaver Brook to Harvard's Prospect and Oak Hills, the Shaker lands on Holy Hill and the Nashua River at Oxbow.

destinations.name: Pioneer Valley
destinations.state_or_region: Massachusetts (Connecticut River valley — Mt. Tom, Holyoke Range, Northampton, Amherst, Mt. Sugarloaf & Mt. Toby)
destinations.agency: MA DCR, Mass Audubon, Kestrel Land Trust, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: Traprock ridges above the Connecticut River: the cliffs of Mt. Tom, the Holyoke Range traverse from Mt. Holyoke's Summit House to Norwottuck and the Horse Caves, and north past Northampton and Amherst to Mt. Sugarloaf and the Mt. Toby fire tower, linked by the New England Trail and the Robert Frost Trail.

destinations.name: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
destinations.state_or_region: Tennessee & North Carolina (Great Smoky Mountains National Park)
destinations.agency: National Park Service, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: The whole of America's most-visited national park: misty ridges along the Appalachian Trail from Fontana Dam to Davenport Gap, Clingmans Dome and Mount Le Conte, old-growth coves, waterfalls, Cades Cove and Cataloochee.

destinations.name: Grand Canyon National Park
destinations.state_or_region: Arizona (Grand Canyon National Park — South Rim, North Rim, Inner Canyon & Marble Canyon)
destinations.agency: National Park Service, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: The whole canyon from Lees Ferry and Marble Canyon to the Grand Wash Cliffs: South and North Rim, the Bright Angel, Kaibab and Grandview corridors, Phantom Ranch and the remote inner-canyon routes. Extreme heat below the rim — a rim-to-river day hike is not recommended.

destinations.name: Yellowstone National Park
destinations.agency: National Park Service, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: The whole park: geyser basins and boardwalks, the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone, Yellowstone Lake, the Lamar Valley and the Absaroka, Gallatin and Washburn ranges. Stay on boardwalks in thermal areas; carry bear spray.

destinations.name: Grand Teton National Park
destinations.state_or_region: Wyoming (Grand Teton National Park & John D. Rockefeller, Jr. Memorial Parkway)
destinations.agency: National Park Service, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: The whole park and the Rockefeller Parkway to Yellowstone: the Teton Range above Jenny, Jackson and the other glacial lakes, Cascade and Paintbrush canyons, the Teton Crest, and the sagebrush flats of Jackson Hole. Carry bear spray.

destinations.name: Joshua Tree National Park
destinations.state_or_region: California (Joshua Tree National Park — Mojave & Colorado deserts)
destinations.agency: National Park Service, USGS 3DEP & OpenStreetMap Contributors
destinations.summary: The whole park where the Mojave meets the Colorado Desert: Joshua tree forests, granite boulder piles, fan-palm oases, the Little San Bernardino Mountains and the wide Pinto Basin. No water in the park's backcountry — carry at least a gallon per person per day.
